# Autonomous task implementation workflow

## Trigger

When the user says something equivalent to "Ponte con la siguiente tarea", "Implementa la siguiente tarea", "Siguiente tarea", "Continúa con el backlog", or any other phrasing (Spanish, English, or otherwise) that clearly means "implement the next backlog task", run the workflow below immediately, without asking the user to repeat or paste it again. The exact wording never needs to match literally — interpret intent consistently.

This trigger means **implement**, never **refine**. Never treat it as a request to work through `backlog/inbox.md` or move a task from `refinement`/`inbox` to `ready` — that is the separate refinement workflow (see [`backlog.instructions.md`](./backlog.instructions.md)) and only runs when explicitly requested.

## Workflow

1. **Read context**: `.ai-context/`, `backlog/README.md`, and the `status`, `priority`, `depends_on`, and `created_at` fields from each task.md frontmatter across `backlog/tasks/*/` to find the `ready` tasks. Only read a task's `specification.md`/`implementation.md` for tasks that pass the readiness, dependency, and tie-break checks from step 2 and are the top 1-2 remaining candidates. If a tie remains after applying all tie-break rules and every tied task has all required fields present, select the task listed first in `backlog/tasks/*/` alphabetically and note the tie in the final report. If any tied task is missing a required field (e.g. `created_at`) or is otherwise ambiguous, do not guess — flag the ambiguity and ask for clarification before proceeding. While awaiting clarification, do not begin implementation on any candidate task, and do not fall back to refining an inbox item automatically — this trigger only implements (see Trigger above). Note: `backlog.instructions.md`'s general ambiguity fallback (proceed to refine an inbox item) applies only to manual/general backlog review, not to this autonomous "next task" trigger — under this trigger, ambiguity always means stop and wait for clarification, never switch to refinement.
2. **Select the task** following the selection rules in `backlog.instructions.md` (readiness, dependency safety, tie-break order) referenced above. Report the selected FIN ID and title before touching anything else.
   - If no task qualifies, stop here: report that there is no eligible implementation task and why (e.g. all `ready` tasks are blocked, or none has `status: ready`). Do not fall back to implementing a `refinement`/`inbox` item, and do not start refining anything unless separately asked.
3. **Prepare Git** exactly as described in [`git.instructions.md`](./git.instructions.md) (clean tree check, fetch, fast-forward `main`, create/reuse the branch, switch). Never implement on `main`. If the working tree is not clean, stop and report the uncommitted changes to the user instead of proceeding, unless `git.instructions.md` specifies otherwise. If the existing branch conflicts with the current task's base or contains unrelated commits, stop and report the conflict instead of reusing it.
4. **Read the task**: `task.md`, `specification.md`, `implementation.md`, the relevant application code, and `.ai-context/` for project-level technical context. If `task.md` or `specification.md` is missing for the selected task, stop and report the missing file instead of proceeding with implementation. Set `status: in_progress` and update `updated_at` in `task.md` before starting.
5. **Resolve `depends_on`** if not all are `done`: assess whether the incomplete work affects the files, APIs, or data structures this task touches. If it's safe to proceed, note explicitly why the incomplete dependency doesn't affect this task before continuing.
6. **Handle blockers**, whether discovered up front or mid-implementation:
   - 6a. If blocked by an unresolved product/architectural decision (do not invent missing requirements), pause, set `status` back to `refinement`, document it as a product-decision blocker in `implementation.md`, and report it instead of implementing further.
   - 6b. If blocked by an unsafe `depends_on`, pause, set `status` back to `refinement`, document it as a dependency blocker in `implementation.md`, and report it instead of implementing further.
7. **Implement** only the selected task's scope (`task.md` + `specification.md`'s "Out of Scope"), following existing architecture, coding conventions, established patterns, testing strategy, accessibility and security requirements. Don't opportunistically implement other backlog items — log a brief note (1-2 sentences describing the observation and file/location) as a new entry in `backlog/inbox.md` instead. Keep `implementation.md` current as you go (approach, files affected, step checklist, decisions).
8. **Validate** using the project's existing scripts (type checks, lint, unit/integration/E2E/accessibility tests, build) for the areas touched — see root README.md and [`testing.instructions.md`](./testing.instructions.md). Don't skip a validation step silently; if one is skipped, document why. If no validation script exists for a touched area, document this explicitly in `implementation.md` rather than skipping silently. Fix failures caused by this implementation before continuing; do not mark the task complete with unresolved failures. If a validation failure is unrelated to this implementation (pre-existing), document it in `implementation.md` and proceed without fixing it, unless it blocks verifying this task's changes. If a validation script fails to run due to environment/tooling issues (not test failures) — e.g. missing dependencies, environment errors — document the error in `implementation.md` and report it in the final report rather than silently proceeding.
9. **Update the backlog**: task status, `implementation.md` (approach, files affected, decisions, validation results), while preserving the original `specification.md`. Only set `status: done` once the Definition of Done is actually satisfied; otherwise leave it in the correct status (`in_progress`, `review`, or back to `refinement`) and document why. If `task.md` has no Definition of Done, or it's ambiguous, do not mark the task `done` — leave it in `refinement` and note the missing/ambiguous criteria in `implementation.md`.
10. **Review the diff** before committing: `git status`, review the full diff, confirm only files belonging to this FIN task are included, and that no generated or temporary files slipped in.
11. **Commit** following the conventions in `git.instructions.md` referenced above — within this autonomous workflow, the commit step is part of the standard flow and doesn't require a separate explicit request each time (`git.instructions.md`'s "only commit when explicitly asked" rule applies outside this workflow). One commit per task unless the repository's conventions require more.
12. **Do not merge** the branch into `main`, and do not push unless explicitly instructed.
13. **Final report**, always structured as:
    - **Task**: FIN ID, title, final status
    - **Git**: branch, base branch, commit hash, commit message
    - **Implementation**: concise summary
    - **Validation**: commands/tests run and their results
    - **Remaining work**: blockers or follow-ups, if any

## Never

The agent must never: work directly on `main`; discard, reset, or stash unrelated uncommitted user changes; invent unresolved product requirements; implement unrelated tasks; merge automatically; silently skip failing validation; or mark a task `done` when it isn't actually complete.
